rule.borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are the ones where the two readings genuinely compete. Every one carries the sentence that decided it, so a human can flip it and rerun.
rule.not_scheme: the money runs, builds, staffs or maintains an organisation or an asset, devolves general purpose funds to another tier of government, buys the capacity of the delivery system rather than the benefit, discharges the state's obligation to its own serving or scheme staff, or is an accounting or adjustment head
rule.scheme: the money buys an identifiable benefit received by a person or household: cash, a kit, food, a scholarship, a fee waiver, a pension, insurance, a subsidy, a loan or its waiver, free power, free travel, a house, treatment for a named beneficiary class, or training in which the trainee is himself the beneficiary
rule.two_lines_that_did_the_work: First, a TRAINING head is a scheme when the trainee is a citizen of a named class and not a scheme when the trainee is the state's own staff: pre-recruitment coaching for unemployed Dhangar youth is a scheme and 'Training to Government Employees' is not. Second, a SATURATION MISSION that improves a habitation is not a scheme even when the habitation is a named community's: Tanda Vasti Sudhar Yojana, PM JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan all build village infrastructure, and all three are the errors that survive publication.
rule.adopted: This is the register's SINGLE definition, taken from the wording the first seven states were labelled against because it is the more carefully drawn of the two that existed. The eight states labelled later used a looser one that admitted 'a service', which pulled in the capacity of a delivery system: a helpline, a creche, an anganwadi's running costs, an agricultural extension wing. 69 published rows were re-read against this wording and 56 changed side. The register's headline number counted two different things before that and said so nowhere.

sampling: Stratified by DEPARTMENT FAMILY (WELFARE, SERVICE, ECONOMY, INFRA, GOVERNANCE, a fixed partition of the 56 departments listed in parse/classify_maharashtra.py) crossed with allocation band (nil, and quartiles of the 1,857 codes that carry an allocation), 25 non-empty strata. The 56 departments cannot each be a stratum: 56 crossed with 5 bands is 280 cells and a sample large enough to fill them could not be labelled by hand. Within a stratum rows are sorted by scheme code and picked at even spacing, so the sample is reproducible without a random seed. Allocation is proportional to stratum size with a floor of 6, so the sample is close to self weighting; stratum_size and stratum_sampled are carried on every stratified row so a weighted estimate can be recomputed.

audit.what: Every row the classifier scores 5 or above that the stratified sample had not already covered. Together the two sets are a census of the published region and of the three bands below it, so the published list's precision is counted rather than estimated. The audit was made after the weights were fixed and was not fed back into them.

stratified.what: A probability sample of all 1,956 scheme codes. This is the only set the threshold sweep uses, because precision and recall estimated on anything else would not generalise to the rows the classifier has not seen.
